label: July 13–19
title: “He Trusted in the Lord God of Israel” —  2 Kings 16

items.text: Despite the prophet Elisha’s powerful ministry, the people of Israel did not repent, leading to their conquest. The Southern Kingdom also faced spiritual decay. Amidst this, Kings Hezekiah and Josiah inspired their people to turn back to the Lord, offering a beacon of hope.

When our lives need reform, we can take encouragement from the bright spots in Judah’s history. The examples of Hezekiah and Josiah can inspire us to trust in the Lord our God, even when faced with overwhelming challenges or spiritual decay.

We can stay true to the Lord when our faith is challenged. Like Hezekiah facing the Assyrian army, we can choose to trust in the Lord, comparing the enemy’s taunts with our personal reasons for faith in Him and His plan.

Hezekiah remained faithful because he trusted in the Lord. He sought the Lord’s help through prayer and relied on the prophet Isaiah. The Lord responded by saving Jerusalem miraculously, demonstrating His power over earthly armies and His love for the faithful.

When facing challenging times, ponder how the Lord has sustained you. What do you feel inspired to do to increase your trust in Him? Resources like President Holland’s message, hymns, and scripture study helps can provide strength and encouragement.

All things are in the Lord’s hands. Even when earthly powers seem formidable, the Lord’s message through His prophets reveals His ultimate power and plan. His truths help us have faith in Him and His divine purposes for us.

The scriptures can turn our hearts to the Lord. When we feel spiritually lacking, the rediscovery of the book of the law, as with King Josiah, can inspire profound repentance and revival of religious life among the people.

King Josiah and his people changed because they heard and obeyed the word of the Lord found in the scriptures. This led to widespread reforms and a renewed commitment to keeping God’s commandments, demonstrating the power of scripture.

President Spencer W. Kimball called the story of King Josiah “one of the finest stories in all of the scriptures.” We can seek to have experiences where a passage of scripture “work[s] mightily” in us, turning our hearts back to the Lord.

When we sense that our lives need some reforms, we can take encouragement from the examples of Hezekiah and Josiah. Their faith in the Lord and their efforts to turn their people back to Him can inspire us to trust in God.
